passages.note: Senate floor final passage of the Senate-amended text (the SAFETY Act), 29-8, Gonzalez Aye; 8 of 37 voting No is above the 10% near-unanimous line.

passages.provision_quote: shall not enact or enforce any policy, rule, or administrative regulation that would require an employee or a contractor to disclose any information related to a pupil’s sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression to any other person without the pupil’s consent, unless otherwise required by state or federal law.
passages.note: Chaptered text is the text the Senate voted on; its operative Section 220.5 forbids school policies that require disclosure of a pupil's gender identity without consent, while Section 220.3 only removes a duty to disclose and does not require staff to withhold.

rows.reasoning: Gonzalez voted Aye on Senate final passage of AB 1955 (2023-2024), 29-8, a single-subject pupil-privacy bill whose operative Section 220.5 says a school district or its board "shall not enact or enforce any policy, rule, or administrative regulation that would require" disclosure of a pupil's gender identity without consent. That matches the rung "Forbid rules that require schools to tell parents"; it does not reach "Require staff to keep a student's gender identity from parents unless the student consents", because the bill only removes any requirement to disclose and imposes no duty to withhold. The rung is itself about which level may set the rule, so the preemption shape is on-question here.
